{{Short description|Quality control expert}}
{{one source|date=May 2014}}
'''George DeForest Edwards''' (1890 – 1974) was a 20th-century [[quality control]] expert most notable for having served as the first president of [[American Society for Quality|American Society for Quality Control]]. 

Edwards' reputation in quality control had been established by his work as head of the inspection engineering department of [[Bell Telephone Laboratories]] and as Bell’s director of [[quality assurance]], a term he coined. During [[World War II]], he served as a consultant to the [[US Army]] [[Weapon|Ordnance]] Department, and later to the [[War Production Board]]. 

Edwards retired from Bell in 1955 but he remained active in ASQ, serving as chair of the Committee on [[Constitution]] and [[Bylaw]]s, and later as deputy executive secretary for dues abatement.
